question: On the basis of Articles 130-142 of Law 5221/2025, Joint Ministerial Decision 42483/2026 was published on 11 August 2026, during the judicial vacations, setting 1-30 September 2026 as the first timeframe for submitting applications for the rescheduling of court hearings on oppositions to payment orders and enforcement orders.

The decision establishes the mandatory rescheduling of hearings on opposition to payment order and enforcement order cases pending at first instance on 15 July 2026 and scheduled for hearing on 17 September 2027: (a) without the submission of an electronic application to reschedule a hearing, the opposition is deemed to have never been filed and the suspension is automatically revoked; (b) the application must be filed within 30 days, otherwise it is deemed to have never been filed; (c) the lawyer who had submitted the opposition is notified, without ensuring that they continue to represent or communicate with the debtor.

For the consumer, this means that an auction could take place before the claim or the unfair terms are checked. Based on judgments C-415/11 Aziz, C-34/13 Kušionová and C-725/19 Impuls Leasing, Directive 93/13/EEC requires effective protection and interim measures to prevent irreversible consequences. With this in mind, can the Commission answer the following: 1.

Does it consider the cumulative penalties, which could potentially result in the dismissal of a consumer’s punctually filed judicial opposition, to be proportionate in the light of Articles 6 and 7 of Directive 93/13/EEC and Articles 7, 17 and 47 of the Charter?

Is effective temporary judicial protection guaranteed when the suspension is automatically revoked and can an auction be concluded before a decision is issued on the opposition to a payment or enforcement order and before any unfair terms have been examined?
Will it ask Greece for information and examine the compatibility of the regulations with EU law in order to prevent homes or property from being irreversibly lost?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (13.10.2026) Council Directive 93/13/EEC1 requires Member States to ensure that consumers are not bound by unfair terms in consumer contracts and that they have effective remedies against such terms including during enforcement procedures2. However, procedures applicable to enforcement procedures, such as on court hearings, must be set out in national legislation3.
The Commission does not have powers to review decisions of national authorities and courts or to order the suspension of property auctioning.

Based on the circumstances of each case, it is the primary responsibility of the national authorities and courts to ensure the monitoring and enforcement of the application of consumer law in individual disputes, to provide interim relief, if necessary to ensure the full effectiveness of the final court decision4 or redress5.

The Commission is constantly monitoring the implementation of the Directive by the Member States, including Greece. It will assess any information pointing to possible infringements of Council Directive 93/13/EEC including as regards its effectiveness and, if appropriate, address the issue with the national authorities in line with the Commission’s enforcement priorities6.
1 Council Directive 93/13/EEC of 5 April 1993 on unfair terms in consumer contracts (OJ L 95, 21.4.1993, p.

29). 2 See Section 5 of Commission Notice – Guidance on the interpretation and application of Council Directive 93/13/EEC of 5 April 1993 on unfair terms in consumer contracts, OJ C 323, 27.9.2019, p. 4–92, COM(2019) 5325 final. 3 See for example CJEU judgment in Case C-509/24, Investcapital Ltd. 4 See for example CJEU judgment in Case C-725/19 Impuls Leasing, paragraph 51. 5 See for example CJEU judgment in Case C-224/01, Köbler. 6 Set out in Communication C(2016)8600.
